sections.label: MAS powers consolidated in Bill
sections.summary: The Bill enhances MAS' regulatory and enforcement framework and consolidates similar powers spread across various Acts into one Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: First, it enhances MAS' regulatory and enforcement framework across the financial sector, besides the rules designed for each segment of the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We will consolidate some of MAS' powers on similar issues, which are currently spread across various Acts into one single Bill.

sections.label: Powers housed under FSM Bill
sections.summary: AML/CFT, FI resolution and dispute resolution powers will be housed under the omnibus Financial Services and Markets Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: These include: one, those relating to anti-money laundering and the countering of financing of terrorism (AML/CFT); and two, the resolution of financial institutions (FIs) in distress and financial industry dispute resolution schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: These powers will now be housed under the Financial Services and Markets (FSM) Bill, which acts as an omnibus Bill.

sections.label: Licensing digital token service providers
sections.summary: The FSM Bill seeks to mitigate reputational risks by licensing DT service providers and imposing AML/CFT requirements on them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: And we could be exposed to reputational risks brought by DT service providers created in Singapore and which provide services relating to virtual assets, such as bitcoin, outside of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: So, this FSM Bill seeks to mitigate such risks by licensing these players and imposing AML/CFT requirements on them.

sections.label: Regulating DT services outside Singapore
sections.summary: The FSM Bill regulates persons in Singapore providing DT services purely outside Singapore, introducing licensing and AML/CFT inspection powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The FSM Bill will regulate all persons in Singapore who conduct a business of providing DT services purely outside of Singapore, if they are created in or operate their businesses from Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The FSM Bill will introduce licensing requirements and general powers over DT service providers, including powers for MAS to conduct AML/CFT inspections and to render assistance to domestic authorities and MAS' foreign AML/CFT supervisory counterparts.

sections.label: Raised penalty for TRM breach
sections.summary: With the FSM Bill's passing, the maximum penalty for each breach of a TRM requirement rises to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: With the passing of the FSM Bill, the maximum penalty for each breach of a TRM requirement will be raised to $1 million.

sections.label: Statutory protection for dispute resolvers
sections.summary: The FSM Bill provides statutory protection from liability for persons mediating or adjudicating disputes who acted with reasonable care and good faith.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The FSM Bill will provide statutory protection for such persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This will strengthen the confidence and autonomy of these individuals when they carry out their duties and align the level of protection for them more closely with that of other public dispute resolution bodies in Singapore and internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: They will be protected from liability if they acted with reasonable care and in good faith in the course of mediating or adjudicating a dispute.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: They will, however, continue to be liable for acts involving wilful misconduct, negligence, fraud or corruption.

sections.label: Licensing digital token service providers
sections.summary: Part 9 of the Bill introduces a regime to license and regulate Singapore-based digital token service providers serving customers outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Part 9 of the Bill, MAS seeks to introduce a regime to license and regulate digital token service providers based in Singapore but who provide digital token services outside Singapore.

sections.label: Penalty for TRM non-compliance
sections.summary: Maximum penalty for non-compliance with TRM requirements is proposed at $1 million plus $100,000 per continuing day after conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Importantly, the maximum penalty for non-compliance with such TRM requirements is proposed to be $1 million plus $100,000 for every day that the offence continues after conviction, to signal the importance of TRM in light of the serious effects of any potential disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This high penalty might have the chilling effect of discouraging FIs from working with fintech startups which typically have small operations and may not be able to invest in layered and complex cybersecurity defences.

sections.label: Harmonised Prohibition Orders power
sections.summary: Part 3 of the Bill proposes a single harmonised power to issue Prohibition Orders barring persons from particular functions in Singapore's financial sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Part 3 of the Bill proposes to introduce a single, harmonised power to issue Prohibition Orders, or POs, to persons to prevent them from performing particular functions in Singapore's financial sector.

sections.label: Criminal offence for employing PO persons
sections.summary: It will be a criminal offence for a financial institution to employ or use the services of a person against whom a PO is made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Importantly, it will be a criminal offence for the FI itself, if it were to employ, or use the services of, a person against whom a PO is made.

sections.label: Public register of Prohibition Orders
sections.summary: The question asks whether MAS intends to create and maintain a public register of POs beyond its Enforcement Actions webpage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is MAS intending to create and maintain a public register of POs beyond the current publication of formal regulatory and enforcement actions taken by MAS on its "Enforcement Actions" webpage?

sections.label: Banking-related phishing case statistics
sections.summary: In 2020, 893 banking-related phishing cases cost victims at least $3.3 million; in the first half of 2021, 535 cases cost at least $2.1 million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2020, there were 893 reported cases of banking-related phishing activities, costing victims at least $3.3 million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And in the first half of 2021, excluding the $13.7 million loss from the OCBC episode, already 535 cases were reported, tallying at least $2.1 million.

sections.label: PayNow safeguards transfer limit test
sections.summary: The speaker and Louis Chua tested PayNow safeguards by transferring sums above the $1,000 daily limit allowed without token authentication.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As I shared with this House in February, my Sengkang colleague, Louis Chua and I conducted a simple experiment where we tested PayNow safeguards by transferring sums in excess of $1,000, the stated maximum daily transfer limit allowed without requiring token authentication.

sections.label: Scam measures and legislative consequences
sections.summary: Measures help thwart scams, but without stricter legislative consequences, costs of breaches fall mainly on the end-user.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These have been deployed to help thwart scam attempts even here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But absent stricter legislative consequences that would spread the costs of breaches and establish a minimum standard of care for retail banking customers, the effects of the inevitable lapses will continue to mainly be borne by the end-user.

sections.label: MAS action in OCBC fiasco
sections.summary: MAS announced possible supervisory actions against OCBC after public outcry, and still permitted SMS for OTPs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the recent OCBC fiasco, MAS only announced possible supervisory actions against the bank, well after the fact, and in the wake of a public outcry over the matter.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And despite well-known security vulnerabilities associated with SMS technology, MAS had continued to permit its use for sensitive functions, such as OTPs or requesting information from customers, and has only advocated the removal of clickable links thus far.

sections.label: MAS scam loss sharing framework
sections.summary: MAS announced a framework for sharing scam losses, but it is not comprehensive and does not cover consumer protection beyond scams.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Back in January, MAS announced a framework for the equitable sharing of losses arising from scams.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is surely welcomed and will provide additional clarity on apportioning fraud-related losses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But the framework is far from comprehensive and does not yet address aspects of consumer protection that go beyond scams.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If the experience of the United States is any indication, passing a consumer financial protection law would likely lead to financial institutions taking much more care to detect and pre-emptively stamp out instances of phishing and fraud, since losses cannot be immediately foisted off to the customer.

sections.label: Financial sector jobs and benefits
sections.summary: The financial sector provides good jobs for over 170,000 residents and led to spin-off benefits in the local economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Global reputation aside, our financial sector provides good jobs for over 170,000 residents and has led to many spin-off benefits in our local economy.

sections.label: Regulation of Virtual Asset Service Providers
sections.summary: The Bill plugs the gap in regulating entities created in Singapore but providing VA services overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the enhanced regulation for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), the Bill will plug the gap in regulating entities created in Singapore but providing VA services overseas.

sections.label: NFT money laundering risks
sections.summary: The Bill enhances regulation of virtual asset service providers for money laundering and terrorist financing, addressing risks to Singapore's financial hub reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, given the rising popularity of NFTs as a store of money and, hence, its susceptibility to being a vehicle for money laundering, such risks can tarnish Singapore’s reputation as a financial hub if uncurbed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In building a strong local banking system, MAS has adopted a pragmatic approach to manage risks and to foster trust without stifling innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am confident that this Bill will continue to strengthen oversight of our financial sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One of the key aspects of the Financial Services and Markets Bill relates to enhancing the regulation of virtual asset service providers for money laundering and terrorist financing.

sections.label: Singapore virtual assets leadership
sections.summary: The speaker urges Singapore and MAS to take market leadership and move expeditiously to facilitate responsible development of the virtual assets industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If 2020 was seen by the industry players as the year cryptocurrencies were institutionalised, then 2022 is perhaps the year when there is growing recognition of the trajectory of growth in the interconnectedness and skill of digital assets and, certainly, its corresponding implications for global financial stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, the first point I would like to raise is that Singapore and, by extension, MAS as the financial regulator, should strive to take a market leadership role and move expeditiously to facilitate the responsible development of the still nascent but rapidly growing virtual assets industry.

sections.label: MAS virtual asset licence approvals
sections.summary: The speaker asks what holds MAS back on approvals or rejections, noting a company received a Dubai virtual asset licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What then is holding the MAS back on approvals or rejections given their wealth of experience gained over the last two years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Shortly after, in March last month, the company was awarded a virtual asset licence from Dubai's recently formed virtual asset regulatory authority and will be helping to set up an international virtual asset ecosystem in Dubai and assist with the development of virtual asset regulations.

sections.label: FSM Bill virtual asset rules
sections.summary: The FSM Bill regulates all virtual asset service providers created in Singapore serving overseas, and introduces powers on personnel, cross-border activities and technology risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MAS has already implemented the so-called “travel rule” since early 2020, and even though many DPT service providers may still be operating under an exemption, many have already progressively requested for originator and beneficiary information to be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I note that under the MAS Notice PSN02 Prevention of Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism – Digital Payment Token Service, value transfers exceeding S$1,500 would require personally identifiable information, such as residential addresses, identity card numbers and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To further clarify, would major payment institutions licensed and regulated under the Payment Services Act be required to be separately licensed once again, now that the FSM Bill will regulate all virtual asset service providers created in Singapore that provide such services outside of Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Getting early into that game means we can have a headstart and better understand its potential benefits as well as its risks.” I would argue that we had a head start, but many other financial centres across the world are fast catching up or arguably have already caught up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is thus important that we remain open-minded and forward-looking in addressing the opportunities and risks in this rapidly evolving area of finance, facilitate the responsible development of the industry here in Singapore while proactively addressing any threats to financial stability.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Concerning personnel, the Financial Services and Markets (FSM) Bill introduces a harmonised and expanded power to bar persons from holding key roles and conducting certain activities in financial institutions for a period of time in cases of serious misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Concerning cross-border activities, the FSM Bill will regulate all virtual asset service providers created in Singapore that provide virtual asset services outside of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Concerning technology risk management, the FSM Bill sets a maximum penalty amount for breaches to IT systems that lead to disruptions in the provision of financial services.

sections.label: Virtual asset ML/TF regulation
sections.summary: The speaker supports measures strengthening AML/CFT regulation of virtual assets given their anonymous nature and money laundering or terrorism financing potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Considering the potential of a virtual asset to be used for money laundering or terrorism financing (ML/TF) due to its anonymous nature, I strongly support the measures to strengthen regulation of this asset class for Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT).

sections.label: Regulating overseas virtual asset services
sections.summary: The Bill plugs the gap by regulating entities created in Singapore that provide virtual asset services overseas as a new class of financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to plug the gap of regulating entities created in Singapore while providing VA services overseas as a new class of financial institutions.

sections.label: Regulation of virtual asset providers
sections.summary: Regulation of virtual asset service providers should consider capital, audits, fund segregation, compliance, management, record keeping and policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Any regulation of virtual asset service providers should be designed to ensure the following points are considered: minimum capital requirements; audit certificate/external assurance of custodial procedures; segregation of customer and operational funds; annual compliance requirements; being managed by a responsible person with adequate experience; proper segregation of participants' assets and private keys from the marketplace's own assets; appropriate record keeping; maintenance of policies and procedures.

sections.label: Tax incentives for green mining
sections.summary: Businesses doing digital asset mining should get tax incentives if they source their own renewable energy, supporting Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To support Singapore Green Plan 2030, I suggest that businesses conducting digital asset "mining", or similar activities, should receive some form of tax incentives if they source their own renewable energy for their activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Such tax incentives will enable Singapore to become a global leader in green crypto-asset mining.

sections.label: Upgrading financial AI tools
sections.summary: Authorities should upgrade IT analytical tools to use financial artificial intelligence to detect criminal activity and exploit funds transfer reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our authorities should upgrade their IT analytical tools to better exploit the potential of financial artificial intelligence to detect criminal activity by persons who are not already of interest to law enforcement, and to take advantage of reports on international funds transfers and large cash transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore ranked highly in all five areas of competitiveness: business environment, human capital, infrastructure, financial sector development and reputational metrics.

sections.label: Fintech labs and investment growth
sections.summary: Global financial institutions set up innovation labs in Singapore, and fintech investments rose nearly six-fold year-on-year since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Global financial institutions have also set up innovation labs in Singapore to tap on the ecosystem here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And fintech investments in Singapore also increased nearly six-fold year-on-year since 2015.

sections.label: FSM Bill regulatory gap
sections.summary: The FSM Bill covers Singapore businesses providing regulated activities outside Singapore, but a regulatory gap exists for advisory services on digital payment tokens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the other hand, the FSM Bill appears to cover Singapore businesses carrying on the business of providing regulated activities outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There appears to be a regulatory gap where a Singapore-incorporated entity carrying on a business of providing advisory services relating to the offer or sale of digital payment tokens outside of Singapore needs to be regulated under the FSM Bill but a Singapore-incorporated entity doing exactly the same activity but carrying on the business in Singapore, need not be licensed.

sections.label: Blockchain innovation and regulation
sections.summary: Blockchain innovation offers secure data records with use cases beyond cryptocurrencies, and MAS pursues both regulatory oversight and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Blockchain technology innovation offers the fidelity and security of data records and there are many useful use cases beyond cryptocurrencies and digital tokens for payments, for example, digitised bills of lading, certificates of origin and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Implementation of these use cases have the potential of reinventing supply chains and dramatically taking productivity to a different level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is good to see that MAS continues on the twin pursuit of strong regulatory oversight and excellence in innovation for the sector.

sections.label: VASP regulation and AML/CFT risks
sections.summary: Asks whether regulation of virtual asset service providers can be enhanced and streamlined to better manage money laundering and terrorist financing risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, can we further enhance and streamline the regulation of virtual asset service providers (VASPs) to better manage money laundering and terrorists financing risks, or AML/CFT?

sections.label: NFT money laundering and terrorism financing risks
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry addresses possible AML/CFT risks through NFTs under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry clarify how the possible risks of AML/CFT through NFTs are addressed under this Bill?

sections.label: Maximum penalty for technology risk lapses
sections.summary: Asks how often the maximum penalty of $1 million will be meted out for technology risk management lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, how often will the maximum penalty of $1 million be meted out for technology risk management lapses?

sections.label: Exceptions to statutory protection from liability
sections.summary: Asks whether there will be exceptions where statutory protection is not in effect even without wilful misconduct, negligence, fraud or corruption, and supports the statutory protection clauses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, will there be exceptions where the statutory protection will not be in effect, even with the absence of wilful misconduct, negligence, fraud or corruption?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support the provision of Statutory Protection from Liability clauses in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will encourage mediators, adjudicators and dispute resolution employees to conduct their duties with greater confidence and autonomy, which are important for successful mediation.

sections.label: Publishing explanations for prohibition orders
sections.summary: Asks why the Bill does not require MAS to publish an explanation for its imposition of POs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My question is this: why does the Bill not require MAS to publish an explanation for its imposition of POs?

sections.label: Publishing committee's written report
sections.summary: Asks why the committee's written report is not required to be published for the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share why the committee's written report is not required to be published for the public?

sections.label: MAS notifying employer of varied PO
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify whether MAS will notify an individual's employer if the individual's PO is later varied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether MAS will also notify the individual's employer if the individual's PO is later varied?

sections.label: Reputational risks and FSM Bill rules
sections.summary: New rules in the FSM Bill, mainly on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing, are proposed due to reputational risks from DT service providers created in Singapore serving overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we recognise that there may be reputational risks to Singapore in respect of DT service providers created in Singapore but that provide DT services overseas – for instance, those involved in digital payment token or cryptocurrency activities, if they are found to facilitate money laundering activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that the new rules, which primarily relate to anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing requirements, are proposed in the FSM Bill.

sections.label: No additional licensing under FSM Bill
sections.summary: A DT service provider already regulated by MAS under the PS Act, SFA or FAA for DT services need not be additionally licensed under the FSM Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Where the DT service provider is already regulated by MAS under the Payments Services (PS) Act, the SFA or the FAA, for provision of DT services, such an entity does not need to be additionally licensed under the FSM Bill.

sections.label: MAS guidelines on DPT marketing
sections.summary: MAS issued guidelines in January stating digital payment token service providers should not market in public areas in Singapore or engage third parties such as social media influencers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: On Mr Louis Chua's suggestions relating to marketing activities of digital payment token service providers, MAS has issued guidelines in January this year outlining that digital payment token service providers should not market their services in public areas in Singapore, or engage third parties, such as social media influencers, to do so.

sections.label: MAS and SPF cryptocurrency enforcement
sections.summary: MAS increased surveillance of the digital tokens sector and set procedures with SPF, which established a Cryptocurrency Task Force in 2018 to monitor cryptocurrency and improve investigation procedures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Don Wee's point on the need for agencies to better identify criminal activity in this space, MAS has increased surveillance of the digital tokens sector, to identify suspicious networks and higher-risk activities for further supervision, and they have established clear procedures with the Singapore Police Force (SPF) for collaborative enforcement action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: To more effectively combat cryptocurrency scams and crimes, the SPF established the Cryptocurrency Task Force in 2018 to monitor the cryptocurrency landscape and also to develop and improve operational procedures in the investigation and seizing of cryptocurrencies and establish working relationships with overseas law enforcement agencies, industry professionals and academic experts in cryptocurrencies.

sections.label: MAS licence applications review progress
sections.summary: MAS has received over 580 licence applications to date and completed review of close to half of them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MAS has received over 580 licence applications to date and has completed the review of close to half of these applications thus far.

sections.label: Maximum penalty for MAS TRM breaches
sections.summary: Courts may impose up to $1 million per breach of MAS' TRM requirements, and multiple breaches could raise the total penalty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: A maximum of $1 million could be imposed by the Courts for each breach of MAS' TRM requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This means that where there are multiple breaches, the penalty that could be imposed by the Courts on the FI could be higher.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This new maximum penalty is a significant increase from the current penalties under the various Acts administered by MAS.

sections.label: PayNow transaction signing rules
sections.summary: PayNow scheme rules require transaction signing via OTPs or other two-factor authentication for transactions above $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: On the experiment relating to PayNow, it is stated in the PayNow scheme rules that transaction signing, through the use of OTPs or other two-factor authentication methods, is required for transactions above $1,000.

sections.label: PO powers for past misconduct
sections.summary: The Bill allows the new PO powers to apply to misconduct that took place before the Bill comes into effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, the new PO powers can be applied to misconduct that took place before the Bill comes into effect.

sections.label: Effective date of POs
sections.summary: A PO takes effect on the date it is issued by MAS under both the present position and the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In response to the second question, the present position and the position under the Bill is that a PO will take effect on the date the PO is issued by MAS.

sections.label: Public record of POs
sections.summary: MAS' Enforcement Actions webpage publishes enforcement actions for five years, except POs lasting longer than five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Currently, the only public "record" of POs issued may be found on MAS' "Enforcement Actions" webpage, where all enforcement actions are published for a period of five years, except POs that are of a longer duration than five years.

sections.label: PO not issued by default
sections.summary: A PO will not be issued by default.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: A PO will not be issued by default.

sections.label: Employer notification of prohibition orders
sections.summary: MAS will notify an individual's employer when a PO is issued and when it is varied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MAS will notify the individual's employer if a PO is issued, and then, correspondingly, also notify an individual's employer if their PO has been varied.

sections.label: Factors for issuing prohibition orders
sections.summary: MAS will generally consider factors such as harm or risks, whether misconduct was one-off or continued, reasons, and public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: On the question of what the threshold of severity is, or how serious the misconduct must be before a PO is issued, MAS will, generally, take into account factors, such as: one, the harm caused or risks posed by the misconduct; two, whether the misconduct was one-off or continued over a period; three, the reasons why the person carried out the misconduct; and four, public interest and policy considerations.

sections.label: Public register of prohibition orders
sections.summary: MAS could consider a public register of POs in future, once the new PO powers take effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat then asked whether, in addition to the current publication of formal regulatory and enforcement actions taken by MAS on its "Enforcement Actions" webpage, MAS intends to create and maintain a public register of POs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This is something that MAS could consider implementing in future, once the new PO powers take effect under the Financial Services and Markets Act.

sections.label: Guidelines on prohibition order powers
sections.summary: MAS will issue guidelines to provide greater clarity on how the new PO powers will be used.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as MAS has mentioned before in its response to the public consultation, MAS will be issuing guidelines to provide greater clarity on how the new PO powers will be used.

sections.label: Announcement of specific date
sections.summary: MAS will announce the specific date in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)

sections.label: Project Dunbar and CBDC payments
sections.summary: Project Dunbar showed FIs could use CBDCs from participating central banks to transact directly on a shared platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: As Ms Janet Ang mentioned, MAS recently collaborated with the BIS Innovation Hub Singapore Centre and several other central banks on a project known as Project Dunbar to explore a common platform for cross-border interbank payments using CBDCs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Very briefly, Project Dunbar proved that financial institutions (FIs) could use CBDCs issued by participating central banks to transact directly with one another on a shared platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This has the potential to reduce reliance on intermediaries and, correspondingly, the costs and time taken to process cross-border transactions, and is part of the journey that MAS has been embarking on with the industry and other central banks over the few years to explore the potential benefits and feasibility of adopting wholesale CBDC for global payments.

sections.label: MAS reviews Acts, possible harmonisation
sections.summary: MAS regularly reviews its Acts, and existing powers may be harmonised in the FSM Bill in future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I was about to say that the MAS regularly reviews its Acts to ensure that the regulation of the financial sector continues to be efficient and effective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: It is possible that some of the existing powers in various MAS-administered Acts may be harmonised in the FSM Bill in the future if MAS is of the view that such an approach would enable it to address financial sector-wide risks more effectively.
